pages.text: "A station!" Pipi called. Bami bounced by the door. An elderly turtle slowly boarded with a walking stick and old leather bag. "I'll watch the winding mountain track beside Dad!" Bami told him.
Ding! The train started. Bami ran along the aisle from the dining car toward the cab. Handles lined the wall, but Bami held none. "I'm fast! I don't need them!"
The mountain track curved. The train leaned with a squeal. Bami rolled to the aisle's end and hit the door. "Ouch..." Their eyes spun. It was scary.
Bami entered the cab with rumpled feathers. Dad looked back. "You rolled. In a swaying aisle, handles first." Bami pouted. "They're such a bother..."
Dad smiled, his foot gripping the big brass handle. "I hold one, too. An engine driver never lets go. A handle isn't a bother—it's a foot that holds me steady." Bami's eyes widened. "You hold one?"
"Be a little engine driver! Hold the handle tight! One, grip it with a foot when you enter the aisle. Two, lean with the train. Three, move one foot, then grip again!" Bami tried at once.

Another mountain bend. Bami gripped an aisle handle with a foot. The train leaned, but Bami didn't roll. The handle held them steady. "Hold the handle tight!" Bami spread their wings above their gripping foot.
The turtle watched from the dining car, bag on his lap. "A little engine driver!" Bami puffed their chest. "I'm not scared when I hold on!" He nodded, gripping his stick. "I'll hold mine tight, too!"
Now Bami followed the steps through every aisle. "One, handle first! Two, lean together! Three, move a foot and grip again!" However winding the track, Bami didn't roll.
At the last stop, Dad came out and lifted Bami high. "You held on without me, little engine driver!" Handles were feet that held Bami steady. Hold the handle tight!
